indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.1.5 Recognise water and air as important natural resources
indicator.objective: Demonstrate ways of making water safe for use

skills.description: Identify common sources of water in the community (river, well, borehole, pond, standpipe, lagoon).
State simple qualities of good drinking water (clear, odourless, free from germs).
Identify ways of making water safe (boiling, filtering, chlorination, adding iodine tablets, using alum, water filters).
Explain simply why boiling makes water safe (it kills germs).
Explain simply how filtering removes dirt particles from water.
State one danger of drinking unsafe water (e.g. sickness, diarrhoea, cholera).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Clear water is always safe to drink.
Boiling water adds medicine to it.
Water from a borehole never needs treatment.
Adding alum makes water taste better, not cleaner.
Only dirty-looking water can make you sick.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common source of water in a Ghanaian community?
hints: Think of places where people fetch water.
A borehole is dug deep into the ground for water.
questions.explanation: A borehole is a common source of water in many Ghanaian communities. Others include rivers, wells, ponds, lagoons and standpipes.
questions.misconception: Only bottled water is a water source.

questions.stem: Which quality shows that water is good for drinking?
options: It is clear and has no smell
hints: Would you drink water with a bad smell?
Good drinking water should be clear and odourless.
questions.explanation: Good drinking water is clear and has no bad smell. It should also be free from germs.
questions.misconception: Clear water is always safe to drink.

questions.stem: Where does water from a standpipe come from?
options: A pipe supplied by the water company
hints: A standpipe has a tap connected to a pipe.
Ghana Water Company supplies it.
questions.explanation: A standpipe is a public tap connected to a water supply pipe. It is a common source of water in many communities.
questions.misconception: Water only comes from rivers.

questions.stem: Which of these makes water safe to drink?
options: Stirring the water with a spoon
hints: Heat can kill germs in water.
What does your family do to make water safe?
questions.explanation: Boiling water kills germs, making it safe to drink. Adding sand, sugar or stirring does not make water safe.
questions.misconception: Boiling water adds medicine to it.

questions.stem: What can happen if you drink unsafe water?
options: You may become sick with diarrhoea or cholera
hints: Unsafe water contains germs.
Germs can make you sick.
questions.explanation: Drinking unsafe water can make you sick with diseases like diarrhoea, cholera or typhoid.
questions.misconception: Only dirty-looking water can make you sick.

questions.stem: Ama fetches water from a well. The water looks clear but has a slight smell. Is this water safe to drink?
options: No, because it has a smell and may contain germs
Yes, because it comes from a well
hints: Good drinking water should have no smell.
Clear water can still contain germs.
questions.explanation: Water with a smell may contain germs. It should be treated (e.g. by boiling) before drinking, even if it looks clear.
questions.misconception: Clear water is always safe to drink.

questions.stem: Which of these is used to make water safe by killing germs?
hints: Chlorine is added to water in some treatment plants.
Chlorine kills germs.
questions.explanation: Adding chlorine kills germs in water. Alum helps particles settle, and filtering with a cloth removes some dirt but does not kill germs.
questions.misconception: Filtering water kills all germs.

questions.stem: Why does boiling make water safe to drink?
options: It adds flavour to the water
It changes the water into vapour
It kills harmful germs in the water
It makes the water look clear
hints: Heat can kill tiny living things.
What happens to germs at high heat?
questions.explanation: Boiling water to a high temperature kills harmful germs. This makes the water safe to drink.
questions.misconception: Boiling water adds medicine to it.

questions.stem: What does filtering water do?
options: It removes dirt particles from the water
It kills all germs in the water
It adds minerals to the water
hints: A filter has tiny holes.
What gets trapped in the filter?
questions.explanation: Filtering removes dirt and solid particles from water. It does not kill germs, so filtered water may still need boiling.
questions.misconception: Filtering water kills all germs.

questions.stem: Name two sources of water in your community.
hints: Where do people fetch water?
Think of a river and a well.
questions.explanation: Common water sources include rivers, wells, boreholes, ponds, lagoons and standpipes.
questions.misconception: Water only comes from one source.

questions.stem: What is alum used for when making water safe?
options: To help dirt settle to the bottom
To change the colour of the water
hints: Alum makes particles clump together.
The clumps settle at the bottom.
questions.explanation: Alum helps tiny dirt particles clump together and settle at the bottom, making the water clearer. It does not kill germs.
questions.misconception: Adding alum makes water completely safe to drink.

questions.stem: Why should you boil water before drinking it?
answer: to kill germs in the water
to make the water safe by killing germs
hints: What happens to germs when water is boiled?
Boiling water makes it safe.
questions.explanation: Boiling water kills harmful germs. This makes the water safe to drink and helps prevent diseases.
questions.misconception: Boiling water adds medicine to it.

questions.stem: State one disease you can get from drinking unsafe water.
hints: Unsafe water contains germs.
One disease is often linked to dirty water in Ghana.
questions.explanation: Drinking unsafe water can cause diseases such as cholera, diarrhoea or typhoid fever.
questions.misconception: Unsafe water does not cause disease.

questions.stem: A family collects rainwater in a barrel. Which is the best way to make it safe before drinking?
options: Boil the water and let it cool
Leave the water in the sun
Stir the water with a clean spoon
hints: Which method kills germs?
Heat is needed.
questions.explanation: Boiling the rainwater kills germs. Letting it cool before drinking makes it safe.
questions.misconception: Rainwater is always safe to drink.

questions.stem: Kojo boiled water for drinking. His friend said, 'Boiling removes the dirt from the water.' Is the friend correct?
options: Yes, boiling turns dirt into gas
No, boiling kills germs but does not remove dirt
No, boiling makes the water taste bad
hints: What does boiling actually do?
Can boiling remove solid particles?
questions.explanation: Boiling water kills germs, but it does not remove dirt particles. Dirt is usually removed by filtering or letting the water settle.
questions.misconception: Boiling water removes dirt.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes filtering water?
options: It removes all germs from the water
It removes dirt particles but not all germs
It adds chemicals to the water
hints: A filter traps solid particles.
Does filtering kill germs?
questions.explanation: Filtering removes dirt particles from water, but it does not kill germs. Germs are too small to be trapped by most simple filters.
questions.misconception: Filtering water kills all germs.

questions.stem: State two qualities of good drinking water.
answer: it is clear and has no smell
it is clear and free from germs
hints: Should drinking water have a smell?
Should it be clear?
questions.explanation: Good drinking water should be clear, free from bad smell and free from germs.
questions.misconception: Clear water is always safe to drink.

questions.stem: Explain why clear water from a stream may still be unsafe to drink.
answer: because it may contain germs that cannot be seen with the eyes
because germs are too small to see, so the water can look clear but still have germs
hints: Can you see germs with your eyes?
Clear does not mean germ-free.
questions.explanation: Water can look clear but still contain germs that are too small to see. These germs can cause diseases, so the water should be treated (e.g. boiled) before drinking.
questions.misconception: Clear water is always safe to drink.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes a simple way to make water safe from a river?
options: Boil the water, let it cool, then drink
Filter the water with a cloth, then drink
Let the water settle, then drink
hints: Which method kills germs?
Filtering and settling do not kill germs.
questions.explanation: Boiling kills germs. Filtering, adding alum or letting water settle only removes dirt; boiling is needed to make it safe from germs.
questions.misconception: Filtering water kills all germs.

questions.stem: A pupil has three water samples: river water, well water and borehole water. Which is the most important step to make ALL of them safe to drink?
options: Pour each sample into a bottle
hints: Which method works for all water sources?
Heat kills germs in any water.
questions.explanation: Boiling kills germs in any water sample, whether from a river, well or borehole. It is the most reliable way to make water safe.
questions.misconception: Water from a borehole never needs treatment.
